newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC'S BURNS BANNED FROM TOUCHLINE FOR A YEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC'S BURNS BANNED FROM TOUCHLINE FOR A YEAR.

text.p: Glasgow Celtic manager Tommy Burns has been banished from the touchline for a year for losing his temper with a linesman and his unsettled Dutch striker Pierre van Hooijdonk may face disciplinary action for playing in a testimonial match.
Burns was banned by the disciplinary committee of the Scottish Football Association (SFA) as punishment for a fit of temper during Celtic's home league defeat by big rivals Rangers in November.
He had to be restrained as he ran down the touchline to dispute a decision with a linesman and was later banished to the stands by the referee.
Burns, who was also fined 2,000 pounds ($3,300) by the SFA, has a history of clashes with match officials.

"Mr Burns was fined 3,000 pounds ($5,000) in October for aggressive behaviour after a match at Kilmarnock in April and he was fined 1,000 pounds ($1,660) before that," head of the SFA disciplinary committee Drew Herbertson said.
Burns' outspoken striker van Hooijdonk could be in trouble for playing in a testimonial for a former team mate in the Netherlands on Sunday.
Van Hooijdonk, who has crossed swords several times with Celtic over the size of his salary, did not request international clearance from the SFA and, as a result, could face disciplinary action.
"At the moment we are still trying to establish the facts of the case," SFA spokesman Sandy Bryson said.
